note: The benchmark page's flat views (benchmark-views ticket 01): one tab per view, each a kind of job the user picks a Lane for, drawn from one board. `boards` lists [source, benchmark] in preference order; the first board the page has rows for is the view's board, and a benchmark name also matches a versioned one (`Terminal-Bench` matches `Terminal-Bench 2.1`), so a new version of a board needs no edit here. `kind` groups the views on the Frontier tab: composite is shown and never counted in the net tier. `why` is curated, says what decision the view helps with, and is not the source's claim; the source's own words are in boards.json. No model, harness or effort is named here: which Lanes a view lists is the catalog's, found at runtime.

views.title: Overall
views.why: The top-level picture: one composite across agents, coding, scientific reasoning and general knowledge. Good for a first cut, never the whole answer.

views.title: Coding agent
views.why: An agent working in a terminal: building, debugging and operating code end to end. The closest board to a delegated coding job, measured at every effort.

views.title: Whole-repo coding
views.why: Moving a whole repository to a new stack: long-horizon edits across many files, checked by the repository's own tests.

views.title: Knowledge work
views.why: Professional deliverables (documents, spreadsheets, analyses) graded against what an expert in the occupation would produce.

views.title: Factual reliability
views.why: Whether a model knows the answer or says it does not, with a penalty for confident wrong guesses. Research and review jobs lean on this.

views.title: Automation
views.why: Multi-step business workflows driven through REST APIs. Evidence for tool-calling jobs, not for clicking through a browser.
